annotation.method: Codex read the complete 18-page source in physical order through Sections 1-7, Lemma 2.1, Theorem 2.2, Algorithms 4.1, 5.1, and 5.2, every numerical experiment, conclusions, and all 22 references; separated the paper's proofs from cited matrix-function theory, heuristic algorithm design, and experiments; audited Mathlib and the exact frozen 44-object NumStability surface; and compiled paired private feasibility proofs for the closest internally proved candidate.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P51 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 34(4), published electronically July 24, 2012

rejected_candidates.reason: The paper's proof is the spectral mapping observation followed by a termwise triangle and denominator bound for the positive Padé weights and nodes. Paired private proofs of its scalar inequality core are 49 N lines and 50 L lines and mathematically identical. This is below the substantial tier threshold, and the frozen library provides no material shortcut.

The logarithm-of-exponential step is explicitly cited to [16, Problem 1.39], while the sharp alpha_p power-series norm bound (2.5) is obtained by applying [2, Theorem 4.2(a)]. The frozen OperatorLog module can replace part of that cited background only in self-adjoint specializations. Requiring N to reconstruct the cited operator-log theorem would make an artificial T1, and supplying the cited inputs leaves only a short summary argument.
The scalar product formula (3.1), first-superdiagonal formula, and their accuracy properties are taken from references [1], [16], and [18]. They are not newly proved P51 results.

Its parameter selection uses the explicitly asymptotic approximation (4.1), previously published square-root and norm-estimation algorithms, and heuristic limits on extra roots. The paper gives an algorithm design and cost count, not an exact correctness theorem suitable for a source-faithful proof task.

The exact product identity is a short repeated difference-of-squares factorization once the square roots are supplied. The paper explicitly says a complete justification of its cancellation-avoidance effectiveness for general matrices is lacking; formalizing such an accuracy guarantee would invent a result.

The transformation-free procedure combines cited Denman--Beavers iteration, estimated norms, tabulated symbolic constants, and heuristic cost tests. No universal correctness or stability theorem is proved for extraction.
The speed and accuracy comparisons are empirical observations, not universal proof claims.

T1.decision: Skipped. The only substantial frozen operator-log theorems correspond to matrix-function background that P51 cites instead of proving. Its own Lemma 2.1 argument is short and receives no substantial shortcut.

T2.decision: Skipped. No internally proved P51 result receives two distinct substantial non-Mathlib shortcuts from the exact compiled library. Theorem 2.2's hard inputs are external citations, not eligible P51 contributions.

T3.decision: Skipped. Lemma 2.1 and the exact part of (5.1) are below the T2 difficulty floor. The harder backward-error and algorithmic claims either import cited theory, use an explicit asymptotic heuristic, lack a complete general-matrix justification, or are empirical.

selection_policy: Use only exact claims and proof content established in P51.
Do not turn cited matrix-logarithm inversion or power-series norm theorems into P51 proof obligations.
Do not convert asymptotic parameter-selection rules or empirical accuracy evidence into exact theorem statements.
Do not invent the general cancellation-avoidance justification that the paper says is lacking.
Assign a tier only after exact private N and L evidence establishes the tier criteria.
